Alex Morrison: Hey team — ran a quick FinOps pass on our spot strategy for the west/eu GPU fleet. Seeing big nominal savings but variance is biting some product owners. Sharing rough numbers and a proposal below, would love quick takes.
Priya Shah: yes pls. can you paste the numbers? curious about interruption rate assumptions.
Alex Morrison: pasted —
```
pool: mixed-gpu-west
on-demand: $1.20/hr
spot (avg): $0.26/hr
observed interruption rate (30d): 11.8%
preempt retry cost overhead: ~0.06/hr (extra work + requeue)
net spot unit cost (incl retries): ~$0.32/hr
true savings vs on-demand: ~73% (but variance stddev ~9%)
```

Jin Park: nice. two quick q's: how are you attributing retries to teams? and what about long jobs that blow up when preempted?

Alex Morrison: current attribution is per-job tag -> chargeback key. But that doesn't capture wasted compute from failed checkpointless runs. Proposal: add an "interruption premium" charge to teams that opt into spot without checkpointing SLA.

Sophie Liu: I like the premium idea. maybe a blended model: teams that run interruptible workloads get a discount but pay a small volatility fee (per-GPU-hour) that funds reserved buffer + re-run costs. e.g. $0.03/GPU-hr premium for high-interruption pools.

Marco Diaz: operationally we can tag jobs with `spot_policy=checkpointed|best-effort|retryable`. Then billing maps policies -> rate. So checkpointed = spot base, best-effort = spot + volatility fee, retryable = spot + higher fee. Simple mapping avoids manual disputes.

Priya Shah: can we forecast monthly $ impact per team? need a confidence interval for execs. Suggest forecast = baseline consumption * (net spot rate) +/- interruption volatility * contingency factor.

Alex Morrison: ran a quick example for a mid-market customer using 10k GPU-hrs/mo:
- baseline on-demand: $12k/mo
- spot nominal: $2.6k/mo
- net spot w/ retries & premium: $3.4k/mo
- realized variance (90% CI): $3.0k - $3.9k
This is the kind of table I want in the chargeback doc.

Jin Park: question on accounting: do we bill internal teams for the realized cost or the expected (booked) cost? If realized, teams might spike unexpectedly when interruptions peak.

Sophie Liu: recommend blended billing on monthly invoice: 80% expected (forecasted) + 20% true-up based on actuals. That smooths monthly churn and forces teams to internalize variance gradually.

Marco Diaz: also add a QoS SLA tag. If a team needs <50ms cold-start or pinned throughput, they should be on Dedicated and charged accordingly. Keeps expectations clear.

Alex Morrison: operational asks: (1) eng-infra to implement `spot_policy` tags + mapping in chargeback ledger, (2) billing to accept a volatility fee column, (3) product to document checkpointing best practices + checklist. Anyone object?

Priya Shah: no objections. I'll flag finance to review numbers and the proposed $0.03/$0.06 buckets. We should run a 3-month pilot before full rollout.

billing-bot: Automated note: chargeback schema PR exists at https://git.internal/r/redwood/chargeback/pulls/42 — please add comments.

Alex Morrison: thanks. I'll draft the pilot plan + sample invoices and share in #eng-infra in 48h. Action items: Alex (draft pilot + sample invoices), Marco (tagging + ledger mapping), Priya (finance review), Jin (edge-case analysis for long-running jobs), Sophie (docs checklist). :thumbsup:

Sophie Liu: +1 and add an example calc in the doc showing how a 20% interruption month affects a team's P&L.

Alex Morrison: will do. closing thread for now — followups in PR/comments.
